I read every file in the listed backend packages and front-end features, plus the REST flow files (`resources/officefloor/rest/api/sheets/{sheetId}/...`) that set the order each endpoint runs in. Nothing was modified. Below, `J/` means `/home/daniel/ui-work/runs/202610271-to/sandbox/officehq-tanstack-officefloor/src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/`, `F/` means `.../src/main/frontend/features/`, and `R/` means `.../src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/sheets/{sheetId}/`.

## Periods
- **`Period` record** (J/period/Period.java:13-67): fields are `name`, `from`, `to` (both inclusive), `closed`, `closedTotal`, `soft`, `cap` and `locked`.
  - `overlaps` means the two periods share a day (:35); `contains` checks a date (:40).
  - `hardClosed()` = closed and not soft (:55). `reopen()` clears `closedTotal` and `soft` (:60).
- **Add**:
  - `ValidatePeriod` (:12-26): name required, at most 200 characters. To-date required. `cap` must match `[0-9]{1,9}` and be at least 1.
  - `BuildPeriod` (:15-26): a blank from-date takes the sheet's today. Refuses a to-date before the from-date, a name already used, or any overlap with another period. Audit line `PERIOD_ADDED ... [cap=]`.
  - `PeriodRepository.insert` stores `added_on` = the sheet's today (:76).
- **Close**: `ClosePeriod.close` (:37-44).
  - Needs `settings.allows("close", role)`. By default that is clerk or steward.
  - Refuses a period that is `hardClosed`. A soft-closed period can be closed and is fixed again.
- **Soft-close**: `SoftClosePeriod` (:25-31). Same "close" permission; refuses if already `closed`. Claims inside it can still change, because `closedOn` ignores soft periods (PeriodRepository:47-50).
- **Period total as of the period end**: `ClosePeriod.fix` (:52-84).
  - Claim statuses are read from the log at `period.to` (`log.statusesOn`).
  - Figures use `ClaimFigure.withLate` at the **sheet's today**, not at the period end.
  - Per person, a claim counts if its `dueBy` is in the period and `countsAsOf(statusThen, …)` is true (Claim.java:320-324: SETTLED, or OPEN/PENDING that is bound or the person is not retired; never deferred now). n/a is skipped.
  - `closedTotal` = sum of the people's totals; it is not trimmed and shared-claim parts are not applied.
  - It also saves `personTotals`, `personCarried` (`carried()` :92-106 plus `personOpenings`), and freezes pool cuts (`frozen.freeze`).
- **Reopen**: `ReopenPeriod` (:18-35). Needs "reopen" permission (steward by default). Refuses a period that is not closed or is locked. Deletes the person totals and carried figures and thaws cuts. The update requires `NOT locked` (PeriodRepository:129).
- **Lock/unlock**: `LockPeriod`/`UnlockPeriod` both check `allows("lock", role)`.
  - `standingRoles` gives "lock" to steward (Settings.java:120-122).
  - "lock" is **not** in `Settings.ACTIONS` (:112), so `ValidateSettings` (:197-200) refuses a "lock" entry. Locking can never be granted to anyone but a steward.
- **Auto-close**: `AutoClosePeriods` (:23-39).
  - Closes every `!p.closed()` period where `Settings.pastGrace(to, today)` (Settings.java:344-346), i.e. `graceDays != null && to + graceDays < today`. Off while grace days are null.
  - Runs in order of to-date, as a hard close at the new today. No role check.
  - Audit `PERIOD_CLOSED ... auto=yes`. Soft-closed periods are never auto-closed, because they already count as `closed`.
- **Caps**: `PeriodCaps.full` (:17-27).
  - The period is the one containing the claim's `dueBy`.
  - `held` = the person's other claims whose current status is OPEN or PENDING and whose dueBy is in that period. Full when `held >= cap`.
  - `CheckPeriodCap` (:14-21) throws "Period X allows at most N open claims per person". It is wired only in `open.POST` and `review.POST`.
  - `CheckClaimPeriod` (:9-12) refuses changes to claims in a hard-closed period. It is used by about 20 claim endpoints.
- **Generate**:
  - `GeneratePeriods.months` (:30-43): one period per month, named `yyyy-mm`. Skips a month whose name exists or that overlaps. Returns the count `made`.
  - `GenerateQuarters` (:19-30): `yyyy-Q1..Q4`, calendar quarters only.
  - `GenerateFiscalYear` (:19-21): 12 months from `fiscalStart()` (default 1).
  - `fiscalYearOf` = `FY` + the year if the month is on or after the start month, else year−1 (Settings.java:63-65).
- **Rollover**: `RolloverFiscalYear` (:47-104).
  - Steward only. Refuses a year that has no periods.
  - Generates the next fiscal year. For each person, the open figure is the claims belonging to old-year periods that were OPEN/PENDING at the last period's `to` and still count. Non-zero amounts are added to the first new period's opening (`OPENING_SET`).
  - If a rollover of the same year still stands, no openings are added again (`rollovers.stands`).
  - Writes `ROLLOVER fy= periods=`, then soft-closes every still-open old-year period (`PERIOD_SOFT_CLOSED`).
- **Undo rollover**: `UndoRollover` (:22-54).
  - Only the steward who made it, only on the same sheet-today.
  - Refuses if no rollover, if already undone, or if any claim (any status) has a date or dueBy in a generated period.
  - Subtracts the openings (a row reaching 0 is deleted), deletes the generated periods, writes `ROLLOVER_UNDONE`, and reports the count.
- **Import openings**:
  - `ValidateImportOpenings` (:15-37): each line is `name,period,amount` with amount matching `\d+\.\d{2}` (so 0.00 or more). Blank lines are skipped. The first bad line refuses the whole import; no lines is refused.
  - `SetImportedOpenings` (:19-48): resolves every person (by name or alias) and every period before writing anything. Then `addOpening` **adds** to any existing opening, writes `OPENING_SET` per line, and returns `added` = number of lines.
  - There is no TakeRollup/AuditRollup step in its flow (R/openings/import.POST.yml).
- **As-of reads**: `RespondWithPeriods` (:22-54) uses `findAllAsOf` from `period_history`. Person totals and carried figures are shown only if the period is closed now with the same `closedTotal`.

## Statements
- **`TakeStatement`** (J/statement/TakeStatement.java:42-114):
  - The as-of date must be on or before today and not before the person was added (:46-51).
  - Each counting claim gets `live.bind(true, figure, late)` (:102):
    - `statedDue` = the floored rate figure, or `settledDue` for a settled claim. A claim already bound keeps its figure (`ClaimFigure.of` returns `statedDue`).
    - `statedLate` = `ClaimFigure.late` as shown now; null for a settled claim or an n/a figure.
  - Claims that do not count are unbound (:104).
  - The due-total is `n/a` when there is no rate today and nothing is fixed. Otherwise it is `capped(total, CutTotals, latest)`.
  - Shared-claim adjustments (`heldParts`/`ownPart`) apply only when the statement is taken now; `shares` is `Map.of()` when as-of (:63).
  - `statementCount` +1, `statedTotal`, `statementDate` (:111). Audit `STATEMENT ... due-total= claims= [asof=]`.
- **Statement lines** are rows from `person_statement`, formatted `"<date> <stated_total>"` and ordered by `statement_date NULLS FIRST, seq` (J/person/PersonRepository.java:138-142). The front end shows them at F/statements/statement.slot.tsx:109.
- **When binding ends**:
  - The next statement unbinds claims that no longer count.
  - `CancelStatement` (:33-38, steward only) unbinds every claim; an earlier figure is not restored; the count goes −1 and the previous statement shows again (`findStatement`).
  - Reassign (Claim.java:79) and split (Claim.java:206) unbind.
  - A sheet-clone copy leaves the binding behind (ClaimRepository copy javadoc, about line 434). A transfer keeps it (ClaimRepository.java:424-429).
  - While bound, a deferral waits (Claim.java:113-121) and the late charge stays `statedLate` (ClaimFigure.java:80).

## Rollup, snapshots, score
- **`Rollup.of`** (J/rollup/Rollup.java:60-119): per person `claimed`, `dueTotal` (`ownPart` plus `heldParts`, `capped`), `overdueTotal`.
  - Sheet totals use `trimmed` (:168-173): with 3 or more figures, drop the single highest and single lowest. n/a dues are excluded.
  - Overdue (:179-182) = `isOpen` and `overdueFrom(dueBy, grade, date) < today`.
- **`changesSince`** (:190-213) writes `ROLLUP`, `TOTALS` and `ALERT` lines (`ALERT` when a person crosses `alertThreshold`).
- **Score** (:162-165): `settled.movePointLeft(2) − 5×overdueCount`, rounded `HALF_EVEN` to a whole number. `settled` = full `withLate` figures of counted SETTLED claims that are not corrections (:94-97).
- **Snapshots**: `AuditSnapshot` (:15-20) runs on every change of today, for each person:
  - stores `person_snapshot(day = old today, dueTotal)`;
  - writes `SNAPSHOT ... due-total=`.
  - The person read model formats them as `"<day> <due>"` (PersonRepository.java:98).
- **SCORE lines**: `AuditScore` (:15-19) runs only while `scoreLog()` is on. One `SCORE ... score=` line per person, for the day being left.
- **Score bands mid/high**: these exist **only in the front end**. `scoreBand` (F/score/score.ts:13-19): HIGH if score ≥ high, MID if ≥ mid, else LOW; blank if either threshold is blank. The server only validates and stores them (ValidateSettings.java:359-367 accepts `-?\d{1,9}`). Nothing checks mid ≤ high.

## Changing the sheet's today
Flow is R/today.POST.yml:
1. `CheckCanChange`: refuses a viewer or an archived sheet.
2. `ValidateToday`: the value only has to parse as a date. Moving backwards is allowed.
3. `CheckTodayPermission` (J/sheet/CheckTodayPermission.java:15-20): `allows("today")`, clerk or steward by default.
4. `TakeRollup`.
5. `AuditScore`.
6. `AuditSnapshot`.
7. `SaveToday`.
8. `AutoClosePeriods`.
9. `AuditRollup`.

**No escalations or reminders are triggered.** Escalation happens only through `RemindClaim` (J/claim/RemindClaim.java:16-24): a manual remind, once per day; it escalates once ever if the previous reminder was at least `escalateAfter` days before today.

As-of and preview are read-only:
- Server: `LoadSheet` applies them only to GET (J/sheet/LoadSheet.java:21-26).
- Client: changes are refused while an as-of date is set, but only in the client (frontend/api/http.ts:20-24).

## Sheet clone and archive
- **`CloneSheet`** (J/sheet/CloneSheet.java:39-81): steward only, to an id never used.
  - Copies settings, permissions, roles, rates and rate versions (including `added_after`), holidays, retired grades, void reasons, templates, people, snapshots, aliases, holds, patrons and pools (SheetCloneRepository.java:33-166).
  - Periods are copied **all open**: no totals or openings.
  - Statements are not copied. Claims are renumbered in the order they were opened. `cloned_from` is set.
  - Audit `SHEET_CLONE_MADE`, `SHEET_CLONED`, then the full ROLLUP and TOTALS lines of the clone.
  - The clone flow has **no `CheckCanChange`**, so an archived sheet can still be cloned.
- **`ArchiveSheet`**: steward only, refused if already archived. Sets `archived_on = today`, which the as-of view respects (SheetRepository.java:46-58).

## Holidays
- `businessDaysAfter` (J/holiday/HolidayRepository.java:56-64): the terms-th day after the date that is not a Saturday, Sunday or holiday; terms ≤ 0 gives the date itself.
- `SaveHoliday` refuses a duplicate date.
- `RefixDueBys` (:15-23) re-fixes a claim's due-by when all of these hold:
  - it is not SETTLED or VOID (so DRAFT, REVIEW and DELETED are included);
  - its due-by was not set directly by a steward (`!isDueBySet`);
  - its due-by is on or after the new holiday.
- The re-fix uses the claim's own `terms`. The flow is wrapped in Take/AuditRollup.
- The front end does not compute due-by at all (F/overdue/overdue.ts:9). It only pre-checks duplicates and the date format (F/holidays/holidays.slot.tsx:34-41).

## Rates
- **Levels**: `RateRepository.ancestors` (J/rate/RateRepository.java:50-66) looks up the parents to `MAX_LEVEL = 3`, then the `cloned_from` sheet and its own chain. `Rate.inForce` (Rate.java:75-97) takes the lowest level that has a rate in force: the latest from-date on or before the date, unless its to-date is before the date.
- **Forward-only**: `save` (:102-122). If from-date ≥ today, `addedAfter = MAX(id) FROM claim`. **That query covers the whole table, not just this sheet.**
  - `forClaim` (Rate.java:57-60): a claim with id ≤ `addedAfter` sees the `replaced` version instead.
  - The `version` number counts saves for the same grade and from-date.
- **Withdraw**: `withdraw` (:129-144), steward only. Restores the previous version and also deletes the last `rate_history` row, so as-of views lose the withdrawn rate as well.
- **As-of**: `findAsOf` (:152-173) rebuilds versions from history. Parent sheets are taken as they are named now.
- **Preview**: `RespondWithPreview` (:29-55). Replaces **all** levels' rates for the grade with one level-0 rate that has no from-date or to-date. Counts unbound OPEN/PENDING claims whose due changes, and returns `count` and `diff`.
- **Validation**: `RateRequest.checked` (:18-32) pct `\d{1,15}(\.\d{1,2})?`, to-date ≥ from-date. `SaveRate` requires a grade on the sheet.
- **Import**: `ValidateImportRates`/`SetImportedRates` take 2–4 fields per line and write `RATE_SET` plus ROLLUP lines per line.

## Grades
- `Settings.GRADES` = A, B, C plus added grades. `isGradeCode` = `[A-Z]{1,3}` (Settings.java:68-73).
- `AddGrade` refuses a duplicate. `RetireGrade` refuses an unknown or already-retired grade.
- `newPersonGrade` falls back to A if the default grade is retired or missing (GradeRepository.java:52-55).
- `MergeGrade` (J/grade/MergeGrade.java:30-66): steward only; cannot merge into a retired grade or into itself. Moves people whose grade today is the merged grade from today on, then rewrites all their grade records retroactively. Writes `GRADE_MERGED`, then per person `PERSON_EDITED` plus ROLLUP lines.

## Settings and policy versions
- **Dated keys and defaults**: floor 1.00, terms 14, late-pct 0.00 (Settings.java:175-182). `valueOn` uses the floor entry (latest from-date on or before the date).
- **`POLICY_KEYS`** = rounding, floor, cap, terms, late-pct, clerk-limit (:96).
- **`versions`/`versionChanges`**: one policy version per history row of a policy key, filtered by `set_on` for as-of (SettingsRepository.java:99-125).
- **`RespondWithPolicy`** (:21-44): a claim's version = how many versions have a null from-date or a from-date on or before the claim's date. DELETED claims are skipped.
- **Permissions**: `allows` (Settings.java:132-136). A viewer may do nothing; restricted acts as clerk.
- **Rounding**: `rounding` (:331-336). The dated mode wins; otherwise half-up before the policy date and half-even on or after.
- **Cap**: `capped` (:358-363) = min(due, max(cap − cut, 0)). n/a is not capped.
- **Grace and lateness**: `overdueFrom` (:170-173) = due-by plus the grade's grace. The late charge in `ClaimFigure.lateAsOpen` (J/claim/ClaimFigure.java:85-99) compounds every full 30 days.

## Server vs front end
- **Server only**: closed period totals, carried figures and openings; rollover; statements (binding and due-total); ROLLUP/TOTALS/ALERT/SNAPSHOT/SCORE lines; due-by and business days; rate preview; policy version counts; the auto-close decision; fiscal-year labels (`fy`).
- **Front end only**:
  - `scoreBand`
  - the open-period due-total and carried figure (`personPeriodDueTotal`/`personPeriodCarried`/`periodDueTotal`, F/periods/periods.ts:60-118) and `classicPeriodDueTotal` (:125-141)
  - `periodClaimCount` (excludes VOID and DELETED)
  - aging buckets (F/aging/aging.ts)
  - consolidated tree totals and name union (F/consolidated/consolidated.ts:92-119)
  - summary period change (`diffDue`, F/summary/summary.slot.tsx:79-88)
  - snapshot compare (F/snapshots/compare.slot.tsx)
  - tag and month totals, rate calendar, `personExcess`
- **Implemented twice (Java and TypeScript)**: `ClaimFigure` ↔ `claimDue`/`lateCharge`; `Rate.inForce`/`forClaim` ↔ `rateOn`/`forClaim`; `Rollup` due, overdue, n/a and `trimmed` ↔ `personDueTotal`/`uncappedDueTotal`/`trimmedSumDue`/`personOverdue`; `Rollup.score` ↔ `personScore`; `ClosePeriod.fix`/`carried` ↔ `personPeriodDueTotal`/`personPeriodCarried`; `Claim.counts`/`countsAsOf` ↔ `counts`/`countedOn`; `Settings.capped` ↔ `personDueTotal`; `rounding` ↔ `roundsHalfUp`; `overdueFrom` ↔ `overdueFrom`; `standingRoles` ↔ `STANDING_RULE` (F/access/access.ts:115-123); `RespondWithPolicy.versionOn` ↔ `policyVersionOn` (access.ts:198); the validators for period cap, rate pct, year and holiday date.

## Differences between the two copies
1. **Grace days for added grades are ignored in the front end.** `lateOf` builds the grace map only for `GRADES = ['A','B','C']` (F/access/access.ts:100,177-179). Java `gradeGraceOn` works for any grade. Overdue counts, late charges and score for people on added grades can differ.
2. **The "today" used differs.** The front end's open-period figures use `late.today`, which follows the preview date. Java fixes the figures at the sheet's real today.
3. **Displayed vs stored period total.** The period list's "Due" for a closed period sums `personTotals` (periods.ts:68), not `closedTotal`. In the as-of view, where `RespondWithPeriods` empties `personTotals`, it shows 0.00. `classicPeriodDueTotal` falls back to the live figure instead.
4. **n/a edge case.** For a bound claim with an n/a `statedDue`, dated on or before today, where the grade has a rate: the front end treats it as kept (not n/a) because it checks `rateOn` (rates.ts:341-344). Java requires `figure != null` (Rollup.java:100-102).
5. **Policy version with no date.** `policyVersionOn` returns the current count; Java `versionOn` with a null date counts only versions that have no from-date.
6. **Validation regexes.** Period cap: front end `^[1-9]\d*$` vs Java `[0-9]{1,9}` and ≥1 (Java accepts "01"; the front end accepts more than 9 digits). Rate pct: the front end has no 15-digit limit.
7. **Forward-only rates after a clone (likely a bug).** Copied claims get new, higher ids but `added_after` is copied unchanged (SheetCloneRepository.java:58-62). So on the clone, forward-only rates apply to copies of older claims. Separately, `addedAfter` is the maximum id over all sheets' claims (RateRepository.java:111).
8. **Code comments vs code.**
   - The `lock`/`reopen`/`unlock` YAML comments say "Only a steward". The code uses the permission matrix; for reopen this can be changed in settings.
   - The YAML for openings import says amounts add to the "carried figure". They are stored as `period_person_opening`, which feeds carried only through `ClosePeriod`/`personPeriodCarried`.

  - Only the steward who made it, only on the same sheet-today.
  - Refuses if no rollover, if already undone, or if any claim (any status) has a date or dueBy in a generated period.
  - Subtracts the openings (a row reaching 0 is deleted), deletes the generated periods, writes `ROLLOVER_UNDONE`, and reports the count.
- **Import openings**:
  - `ValidateImportOpenings` (:15-37): each line is `name,period,amount` with amount matching `\d+\.\d{2}` (so 0.00 or more). Blank lines are skipped. The first bad line refuses the whole import; no lines is refused.
  - `SetImportedOpenings` (:19-48): resolves every person (by name or alias) and every period before writing anything. Then `addOpening` **adds** to any existing opening, writes `OPENING_SET` per line, and returns `added` = number of lines.
  - There is no TakeRollup/AuditRollup step in its flow (R/openings/import.POST.yml).
- **As-of reads**: `RespondWithPeriods` (:22-54) uses `findAllAsOf` from `period_history`. Person totals and carried figures are shown only if the period is closed now with the same `closedTotal`.

## Statements
- **`TakeStatement`** (J/statement/TakeStatement.java:42-114):
  - The as-of date must be on or before today and not before the person was added (:46-51).
  - Each counting claim gets `live.bind(true, figure, late)` (:102):
    - `statedDue` = the floored rate figure, or `settledDue` for a settled claim. A claim already bound keeps its figure (`ClaimFigure.of` returns `statedDue`).
    - `statedLate` = `ClaimFigure.late` as shown now; null for a settled claim or an n/a figure.
  - Claims that do not count are unbound (:104).
  - The due-total is `n/a` when there is no rate today and nothing is fixed. Otherwise it is `capped(total, CutTotals, latest)`.
  - Shared-claim adjustments (`heldParts`/`ownPart`) apply only when the statement is taken now; `shares` is `Map.of()` when as-of (:63).
  - `statementCount` +1, `statedTotal`, `statementDate` (:111). Audit `STATEMENT ... due-total= claims= [asof=]`.
- **Statement lines** are rows from `person_statement`, formatted `"<date> <stated_total>"` and ordered by `statement_date NULLS FIRST, seq` (J/person/PersonRepository.java:138-142). The front end shows them at F/statements/statement.slot.tsx:109.
- **When binding ends**:
  - The next statement unbinds claims that no longer count.
  - `CancelStatement` (:33-38, steward only) unbinds every claim; an earlier figure is not restored; the count goes −1 and the previous statement shows again (`findStatement`).
  - Reassign (Claim.java:79) and split (Claim.java:206) unbind.
  - A sheet-clone copy leaves the binding behind (ClaimRepository copy javadoc, about line 434). A transfer keeps it (ClaimRepository.java:424-429).
  - While bound, a deferral waits (Claim.java:113-121) and the late charge stays `statedLate` (ClaimFigure.java:80).

## Rollup, snapshots, score
- **`Rollup.of`** (J/rollup/Rollup.java:60-119): per person `claimed`, `dueTotal` (`ownPart` plus `heldParts`, `capped`), `overdueTotal`.
  - Sheet totals use `trimmed` (:168-173): with 3 or more figures, drop the single highest and single lowest. n/a dues are excluded.
  - Overdue (:179-182) = `isOpen` and `overdueFrom(dueBy, grade, date) < today`.
- **`changesSince`** (:190-213) writes `ROLLUP`, `TOTALS` and `ALERT` lines (`ALERT` when a person crosses `alertThreshold`).
- **Score** (:162-165): `settled.movePointLeft(2) − 5×overdueCount`, rounded `HALF_EVEN` to a whole number. `settled` = full `withLate` figures of counted SETTLED claims that are not corrections (:94-97).
- **Snapshots**: `AuditSnapshot` (:15-20) runs on every change of today, for each person:
  - stores `person_snapshot(day = old today, dueTotal)`;
  - writes `SNAPSHOT ... due-total=`.
  - The person read model formats them as `"<day> <due>"` (PersonRepository.java:98).
- **SCORE lines**: `AuditScore` (:15-19) runs only while `scoreLog()` is on. One `SCORE ... score=` line per person, for the day being left.
- **Score bands mid/high**: these exist **only in the front end**. `scoreBand` (F/score/score.ts:13-19): HIGH if score ≥ high, MID if ≥ mid, else LOW; blank if either threshold is blank. The server only validates and stores them (ValidateSettings.java:359-367 accepts `-?\d{1,9}`). Nothing checks mid ≤ high.

## Changing the sheet's today
Flow is R/today.POST.yml:
1. `CheckCanChange`: refuses a viewer or an archived sheet.
2. `ValidateToday`: the value only has to parse as a date. Moving backwards is allowed.
3. `CheckTodayPermission` (J/sheet/CheckTodayPermission.java:15-20): `allows("today")`, clerk or steward by default.
4. `TakeRollup`.
5. `AuditScore`.
6. `AuditSnapshot`.
7. `SaveToday`.
8. `AutoClosePeriods`.
9. `AuditRollup`.

**No escalations or reminders are triggered.** Escalation happens only through `RemindClaim` (J/claim/RemindClaim.java:16-24): a manual remind, once per day; it escalates once ever if the previous reminder was at least `escalateAfter` days before today.

As-of and preview are read-only:
- Server: `LoadSheet` applies them only to GET (J/sheet/LoadSheet.java:21-26).
- Client: changes are refused while an as-of date is set, but only in the client (frontend/api/http.ts:20-24).

## Sheet clone and archive
- **`CloneSheet`** (J/sheet/CloneSheet.java:39-81): steward only, to an id never used.
  - Copies settings, permissions, roles, rates and rate versions (including `added_after`), holidays, retired grades, void reasons, templates, people, snapshots, aliases, holds, patrons and pools (SheetCloneRepository.java:33-166).
  - Periods are copied **all open**: no totals or openings.
  - Statements are not copied. Claims are renumbered in the order they were opened. `cloned_from` is set.
  - Audit `SHEET_CLONE_MADE`, `SHEET_CLONED`, then the full ROLLUP and TOTALS lines of the clone.
  - The clone flow has **no `CheckCanChange`**, so an archived sheet can still be cloned.
- **`ArchiveSheet`**: steward only, refused if already archived. Sets `archived_on = today`, which the as-of view respects (SheetRepository.java:46-58).

## Holidays
- `businessDaysAfter` (J/holiday/HolidayRepository.java:56-64): the terms-th day after the date that is not a Saturday, Sunday or holiday; terms ≤ 0 gives the date itself.
- `SaveHoliday` refuses a duplicate date.
- `RefixDueBys` (:15-23) re-fixes a claim's due-by when all of these hold:
  - it is not SETTLED or VOID (so DRAFT, REVIEW and DELETED are included);
  - its due-by was not set directly by a steward (`!isDueBySet`);
  - its due-by is on or after the new holiday.
- The re-fix uses the claim's own `terms`. The flow is wrapped in Take/AuditRollup.
- The front end does not compute due-by at all (F/overdue/overdue.ts:9). It only pre-checks duplicates and the date format (F/holidays/holidays.slot.tsx:34-41).

## Rates
- **Levels**: `RateRepository.ancestors` (J/rate/RateRepository.java:50-66) looks up the parents to `MAX_LEVEL = 3`, then the `cloned_from` sheet and its own chain. `Rate.inForce` (Rate.java:75-97) takes the lowest level that has a rate in force: the latest from-date on or before the date, unless its to-date is before the date.
- **Forward-only**: `save` (:102-122). If from-date ≥ today, `addedAfter = MAX(id) FROM claim`. **That query covers the whole table, not just this sheet.**
  - `forClaim` (Rate.java:57-60): a claim with id ≤ `addedAfter` sees the `replaced` version instead.
  - The `version` number counts saves for the same grade and from-date.
- **Withdraw**: `withdraw` (:129-144), steward only. Restores the previous version and also deletes the last `rate_history` row, so as-of views lose the withdrawn rate as well.
- **As-of**: `findAsOf` (:152-173) rebuilds versions from history. Parent sheets are taken as they are named now.
- **Preview**: `RespondWithPreview` (:29-55). Replaces **all** levels' rates for the grade with one level-0 rate that has no from-date or to-date. Counts unbound OPEN/PENDING claims whose due changes, and returns `count` and `diff`.
- **Validation**: `RateRequest.checked` (:18-32) pct `\d{1,15}(\.\d{1,2})?`, to-date ≥ from-date. `SaveRate` requires a grade on the sheet.
- **Import**: `ValidateImportRates`/`SetImportedRates` take 2–4 fields per line and write `RATE_SET` plus ROLLUP lines per line.

## Grades
- `Settings.GRADES` = A, B, C plus added grades. `isGradeCode` = `[A-Z]{1,3}` (Settings.java:68-73).
- `AddGrade` refuses a duplicate. `RetireGrade` refuses an unknown or already-retired grade.
- `newPersonGrade` falls back to A if the default grade is retired or missing (GradeRepository.java:52-55).
- `MergeGrade` (J/grade/MergeGrade.java:30-66): steward only; cannot merge into a retired grade or into itself. Moves people whose grade today is the merged grade from today on, then rewrites all their grade records retroactively. Writes `GRADE_MERGED`, then per person `PERSON_EDITED` plus ROLLUP lines.

## Settings and policy versions
- **Dated keys and defaults**: floor 1.00, terms 14, late-pct 0.00 (Settings.java:175-182). `valueOn` uses the floor entry (latest from-date on or before the date).
- **`POLICY_KEYS`** = rounding, floor, cap, terms, late-pct, clerk-limit (:96).
- **`versions`/`versionChanges`**: one policy version per history row of a policy key, filtered by `set_on` for as-of (SettingsRepository.java:99-125).
- **`RespondWithPolicy`** (:21-44): a claim's version = how many versions have a null from-date or a from-date on or before the claim's date. DELETED claims are skipped.
- **Permissions**: `allows` (Settings.java:132-136). A viewer may do nothing; restricted acts as clerk.
- **Rounding**: `rounding` (:331-336). The dated mode wins; otherwise half-up before the policy date and half-even on or after.
- **Cap**: `capped` (:358-363) = min(due, max(cap − cut, 0)). n/a is not capped.
- **Grace and lateness**: `overdueFrom` (:170-173) = due-by plus the grade's grace. The late charge in `ClaimFigure.lateAsOpen` (J/claim/ClaimFigure.java:85-99) compounds every full 30 days.

## Server vs front end
- **Server only**: closed period totals, carried figures and openings; rollover; statements (binding and due-total); ROLLUP/TOTALS/ALERT/SNAPSHOT/SCORE lines; due-by and business days; rate preview; policy version counts; the auto-close decision; fiscal-year labels (`fy`).
- **Front end only**:
  - `scoreBand`
  - the open-period due-total and carried figure (`personPeriodDueTotal`/`personPeriodCarried`/`periodDueTotal`, F/periods/periods.ts:60-118) and `classicPeriodDueTotal` (:125-141)
  - `periodClaimCount` (excludes VOID and DELETED)
  - aging buckets (F/aging/aging.ts)
  - consolidated tree totals and name union (F/consolidated/consolidated.ts:92-119)
  - summary period change (`diffDue`, F/summary/summary.slot.tsx:79-88)
  - snapshot compare (F/snapshots/compare.slot.tsx)
  - tag and month totals, rate calendar, `personExcess`
- **Implemented twice (Java and TypeScript)**: `ClaimFigure` ↔ `claimDue`/`lateCharge`; `Rate.inForce`/`forClaim` ↔ `rateOn`/`forClaim`; `Rollup` due, overdue, n/a and `trimmed` ↔ `personDueTotal`/`uncappedDueTotal`/`trimmedSumDue`/`personOverdue`; `Rollup.score` ↔ `personScore`; `ClosePeriod.fix`/`carried` ↔ `personPeriodDueTotal`/`personPeriodCarried`; `Claim.counts`/`countsAsOf` ↔ `counts`/`countedOn`; `Settings.capped` ↔ `personDueTotal`; `rounding` ↔ `roundsHalfUp`; `overdueFrom` ↔ `overdueFrom`; `standingRoles` ↔ `STANDING_RULE` (F/access/access.ts:115-123); `RespondWithPolicy.versionOn` ↔ `policyVersionOn` (access.ts:198); the validators for period cap, rate pct, year and holiday date.

## Differences between the two copies
1. **Grace days for added grades are ignored in the front end.** `lateOf` builds the grace map only for `GRADES = ['A','B','C']` (F/access/access.ts:100,177-179). Java `gradeGraceOn` works for any grade. Overdue counts, late charges and score for people on added grades can differ.
2. **The "today" used differs.** The front end's open-period figures use `late.today`, which follows the preview date. Java fixes the figures at the sheet's real today.
3. **Displayed vs stored period total.** The period list's "Due" for a closed period sums `personTotals` (periods.ts:68), not `closedTotal`. In the as-of view, where `RespondWithPeriods` empties `personTotals`, it shows 0.00. `classicPeriodDueTotal` falls back to the live figure instead.
4. **n/a edge case.** For a bound claim with an n/a `statedDue`, dated on or before today, where the grade has a rate: the front end treats it as kept (not n/a) because it checks `rateOn` (rates.ts:341-344). Java requires `figure != null` (Rollup.java:100-102).
5. **Policy version with no date.** `policyVersionOn` returns the current count; Java `versionOn` with a null date counts only versions that have no from-date.
6. **Validation regexes.** Period cap: front end `^[1-9]\d*$` vs Java `[0-9]{1,9}` and ≥1 (Java accepts "01"; the front end accepts more than 9 digits). Rate pct: the front end has no 15-digit limit.
7. **Forward-only rates after a clone (likely a bug).** Copied claims get new, higher ids but `added_after` is copied unchanged (SheetCloneRepository.java:58-62). So on the clone, forward-only rates apply to copies of older claims. Separately, `addedAfter` is the maximum id over all sheets' claims (RateRepository.java:111).
8. **Code comments vs code.**
   - The `lock`/`reopen`/`unlock` YAML comments say "Only a steward". The code uses the permission matrix; for reopen this can be changed in settings.
   - The YAML for openings import says amounts add to the "carried figure". They are stored as `period_person_opening`, which feeds carried only through `ClosePeriod`/`personPeriodCarried`.

content.text:
Nothing was changed. I read the figure code myself (`Claim`, `ClaimFigure`, `Settings`, `Person`, `Rollup`, and the front-end `rates.ts`, `claims.ts`, `people.ts`, header, overdue, aging, score, active). Three read-only helpers covered the rules for claim actions, periods, statements and rates, and people; I spot-checked a few of their findings and they held. Paths: **J/** = `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/`, **F/** = `src/main/frontend/features/`.

## 1. Figures and the rules behind them

### Claim figures
The server sends only stored fields. Every live claim figure is worked out in the browser (`F/rates/rates.ts`), and the server repeats the same logic in `J/claim/ClaimFigure.java`.

**`claim-due`** (`claimDue` / `ClaimFigure.withLate`):
- **Settled claim:** the stored `settledDue`. It was frozen at settle or approve and includes the late charge.
- **Otherwise, the rate figure** (`ClaimFigure.of`):
  - If a statement binds the claim (`isBound`, i.e. `stated`), it is `statedDue`. That can be n/a.
  - If not, it is amount × rate ÷ 100, rounded to two places, then raised to at least the `floor` in force on the claim's date (default 1.00).
  - The rate is `Rate.inForce` / `rateOn`: the rate of the person's grade in force on the claim's date (`gradeOn`). It looks at the sheet first, then up to `MAX_LEVEL = 3` parent sheets, then the sheet it was cloned from.
  - A forward-only rate (from-date ≥ today) applies only to claims with an id above `addedAfter`. Older claims see the version it `replaced`.
  - No rate means **n/a**, and n/a gets no floor.
  - A **correction** (negative amount, `corrects`) gets no floor and no late charge.
- **Then the late charge is added** (`late` / `lateAsOpen` / `lateCharge`):
  - Only for OPEN or PENDING claims that are not deferred and not `waived`.
  - Counting starts at `overdueFrom` = `dueBy` plus the grace days of the claim's grade (`grace-<G>`) in force on its date.
  - For every full 30 days overdue, it adds `late-pct` (as in force on that boundary date) of the figure plus the earlier charges. So it compounds, and each step is rounded.
  - If the claim is bound, the charge is fixed at `statedLate` instead.

**Rounding** (`Settings.rounding` / `roundsHalfUp`):
- If a dated `rounding` mode is in force on the claim's round date, that mode is used.
- Otherwise it is half-up before `policyDate` (or the sheet's today if no policy date is set) and half-even on or after it.
- A correction rounds by `correctedDate`, the date of the claim it corrects (`getRoundDate`).

**Other claim fields:**
- **`claim-due-by`:** fixed once when the claim is made (`fixDueBy`) as the terms-th business day after its date, skipping weekends and holidays (`businessDaysAfter`).
  - Terms come from `termsFor`: the person's own terms, else the grade's `terms-<G>`, else the sheet's `terms` (default 14), all as in force on the sheet's today when the claim is made.
  - A redate or edit keeps the due-by.
  - `RefixDueBys` re-fixes it when a holiday on or before it is added, unless the claim is SETTLED or VOID, or a steward set it directly (`dueBySet`).
- **`claim-overdue`** (`isOverdue`): OPEN or PENDING, not deferred, and `overdueFrom` is before today.
- **`claim-number`:** given only when the claim is settled or approved (`ClaimNumbers.giveOnSettle`). The number is never reused, and a voided claim keeps it.
  - The format is `FY<yyyy>-n` by `fiscalYearOf(dueBy)`.
  - When `periodNumberingFrom` is set and today is on or after it, the format is `<period>-n`, or `X-n` if the claim falls in no period.
  - Reassigning renumbers a claim that already has a number.
- **Statement-bound fields:** `claim-stated`, `statedDue`, `statedLate`.
- **Other displayed fields:** `claim-deferred-until`, `claim-held`, `claim-waived`, `claim-late-entry`, `claim-proofs` (receipt/photo), `claim-policy` (`policyVersionOn`: how many policy versions are from on or before the claim's date), `claim-period` (the period containing its due-by), `claim-review-late` / `claim-pending-late` (`reviewSla` / `pendingSla`), and `claim-split-from`.
- **Shared claims:** a holder's part is amount × share × the holder's own grade rate, rounded like the claim. On a settled claim the parts are frozen at due × share, rounded half-even (`holderPart`, `ClaimShare.partOf`).

### Which claims count (`counts`, `countsClaimed`, `countsAsOf`/`countedOn`)
- Counted: SETTLED, OPEN and PENDING.
- Never counted: DRAFT, REVIEW, VOID or DELETED, or any claim `isDeferredOn(today)`. Deferral only applies while the claim is unbound.
- An unbound OPEN or PENDING claim stops counting once its person's retirement date is reached (`Person.heldOn(date, today)` returns `retiredOn(today)`; the front end uses `liveHolds`).
- **A hold (on the person or on the claim) does not take anything out of the totals.** It only zeroes the person's pool cut.
- `counts` and `countsClaimed` are documented as different but are identical in both Java and TypeScript.

### Person figures (all worked out in the front end; the server repeats some of them in `Rollup.of` for audit lines)
- **`person-claimed`** (`sumAmounts`): the amounts of counting claims, excluding corrections.
- **`person-due-total`** (`personDueTotal`):
  - The sum of counting claims' dues, skipping n/a, using the person's own part of shared claims plus parts they hold of others' claims (`heldParts`).
  - It is **n/a** when their grade today has no rate and no counting claim keeps a figure. A claim keeps one if it is settled or bound, has a figure under a different grade, or is dated on or before today with a rate.
  - It is capped (`capped`/`capFor`) at the `cap` in force on the date of their latest counting claim, minus their cut total, never below 0.
- **`person-excess`:** uncapped due + cut − cap, never below 0.
- **`person-settled-total`** / **`person-open-total`** (`personSplitTotals`): before the cap.
- **`person-overdue-count`** / **`-total`** (`personOverdue`).
- **`person-aged-0-30/31-60/61`** (`personAged`): by days from the claim's date.
- **`person-score`** (`personScore` / `Rollup.score`): settled non-correction due ÷ 100, minus 5 per overdue claim, rounded half-even.
- **`person-band`:** front end only. HIGH or MID by `score-high` / `score-mid`, else LOW.
- **`person-active`:** an open counting claim dated in the last 30 days.
- **`person-cut-total`** (pools and crews):
  - A pool is balanced when its active members' shares total 100.00.
  - Each member gets pot × share, rounded half-even, with the remainder going to the smallest cut.
  - Held or retired members get 0.00.
  - Cuts are frozen when a period closes.
- **`person-backing`** (patrons): settled dues from the last 90 days × the patron share. This one ignores `counts`. Patron shares split 100.00 equally, with the remainder going to the first.
- **Taken straight from the server:** `person-statement-count`, `person-stated-total`, `person-statement-date`, the statement lines, the snapshot lines, `person-flag-shown`, retired / retired-from, and grade / terms in force today.

### Sheet totals
- `header-due-total`, `header-overdue-total` and `rollup-*` use `trimmedSumDue` (Java `Rollup.trimmed`): with three or more people, the single highest and lowest are left out.
- The aging totals are a plain sum.
- The consolidated totals cover the whole sheet tree and are trimmed once over.

### Who may do what
- **The permission matrix** is `Settings.allows`, read from `perm-<action>` settings.
  - The default (`standingRoles`) lets clerk and steward do open, settle, void, close and today.
  - Reassign, reopen and lock are steward only by default.
  - A viewer may do nothing (`CheckCanChange`; an archived sheet is refused the same way). A restricted user acts as a clerk.
  - A delegation makes someone a steward while it covers today.
- **Steward only, hard-coded:** flag, merge and undo, transfer and undo, cancel statement, review and review-assign, redate, resettle, set due-by, waive, void a SETTLED claim, merge grades, clone, archive, rollover, withdraw a rate.
- **Settle:**
  - Refused for the user who opened or last edited the claim (`isOwnedBy`).
  - Needs proof when the due is above `proof-threshold(-<G>)`, and one of each `proof-kinds` when those are set.
  - A clerk or restricted user settling above the clerk limit (`clerk-limit(-<G>)`, as on the claim's date) makes the claim PENDING instead.
  - A steward, or the person's `approver`, then approves (the due is frozen) or rejects (back to OPEN).
- **Open:**
  - Refused if the due is above `note-threshold` and the note is blank.
  - Refused if the person already has `max-open` OPEN or PENDING claims.
  - Refused if the period `cap` (open claims per person per period) is reached.

### Claim figures
The server sends only stored fields. Every live claim figure is worked out in the browser (`F/rates/rates.ts`), and the server repeats the same logic in `J/claim/ClaimFigure.java`.

**`claim-due`** (`claimDue` / `ClaimFigure.withLate`):
- **Settled claim:** the stored `settledDue`. It was frozen at settle or approve and includes the late charge.
- **Otherwise, the rate figure** (`ClaimFigure.of`):
  - If a statement binds the claim (`isBound`, i.e. `stated`), it is `statedDue`. That can be n/a.
  - If not, it is amount × rate ÷ 100, rounded to two places, then raised to at least the `floor` in force on the claim's date (default 1.00).
  - The rate is `Rate.inForce` / `rateOn`: the rate of the person's grade in force on the claim's date (`gradeOn`). It looks at the sheet first, then up to `MAX_LEVEL = 3` parent sheets, then the sheet it was cloned from.
  - A forward-only rate (from-date ≥ today) applies only to claims with an id above `addedAfter`. Older claims see the version it `replaced`.
  - No rate means **n/a**, and n/a gets no floor.
  - A **correction** (negative amount, `corrects`) gets no floor and no late charge.
- **Then the late charge is added** (`late` / `lateAsOpen` / `lateCharge`):
  - Only for OPEN or PENDING claims that are not deferred and not `waived`.
  - Counting starts at `overdueFrom` = `dueBy` plus the grace days of the claim's grade (`grace-<G>`) in force on its date.
  - For every full 30 days overdue, it adds `late-pct` (as in force on that boundary date) of the figure plus the earlier charges. So it compounds, and each step is rounded.
  - If the claim is bound, the charge is fixed at `statedLate` instead.

**Rounding** (`Settings.rounding` / `roundsHalfUp`):
- If a dated `rounding` mode is in force on the claim's round date, that mode is used.
- Otherwise it is half-up before `policyDate` (or the sheet's today if no policy date is set) and half-even on or after it.
- A correction rounds by `correctedDate`, the date of the claim it corrects (`getRoundDate`).

**Other claim fields:**
- **`claim-due-by`:** fixed once when the claim is made (`fixDueBy`) as the terms-th business day after its date, skipping weekends and holidays (`businessDaysAfter`).

- **`claim-overdue`** (`isOverdue`): OPEN or PENDING, not deferred, and `overdueFrom` is before today.
- **`claim-number`:** given only when the claim is settled or approved (`ClaimNumbers.giveOnSettle`). The number is never reused, and a voided claim keeps it.
  - The format is `FY<yyyy>-n` by `fiscalYearOf(dueBy)`.
  - When `periodNumberingFrom` is set and today is on or after it, the format is `<period>-n`, or `X-n` if the claim falls in no period.
  - Reassigning renumbers a claim that already has a number.
- **Statement-bound fields:** `claim-stated`, `statedDue`, `statedLate`.
- **Other displayed fields:** `claim-deferred-until`, `claim-held`, `claim-waived`, `claim-late-entry`, `claim-proofs` (receipt/photo), `claim-policy` (`policyVersionOn`: how many policy versions are from on or before the claim's date), `claim-period` (the period containing its due-by), `claim-review-late` / `claim-pending-late` (`reviewSla` / `pendingSla`), and `claim-split-from`.

### Which claims count (`counts`, `countsClaimed`, `countsAsOf`/`countedOn`)
- Counted: SETTLED, OPEN and PENDING.
- Never counted: DRAFT, REVIEW, VOID or DELETED, or any claim `isDeferredOn(today)`. Deferral only applies while the claim is unbound.
- An unbound OPEN or PENDING claim stops counting once its person's retirement date is reached (`Person.heldOn(date, today)` returns `retiredOn(today)`; the front end uses `liveHolds`).
- **A hold (on the person or on the claim) does not take anything out of the totals.** It only zeroes the person's pool cut.
- `counts` and `countsClaimed` are documented as different but are identical in both Java and TypeScript.

### Person figures (all worked out in the front end; the server repeats some of them in `Rollup.of` for audit lines)
- **`person-claimed`** (`sumAmounts`): the amounts of counting claims, excluding corrections.
- **`person-due-total`** (`personDueTotal`):
  - The sum of counting claims' dues, skipping n/a, using the person's own part of shared claims plus parts they hold of others' claims (`heldParts`).
  - It is **n/a** when their grade today has no rate and no counting claim keeps a figure. A claim keeps one if it is settled or bound, has a figure under a different grade, or is dated on or before today with a rate.
